text: Pentagon Mountain is an 8,873-foot (2,704-metre) summit located in Flathead County, Montana. It is the highest point in the Trilobite Range, a portion of the Flathead Range, and lies within the Bob Marshall Wilderness, managed by Flathead National Forest. The mountain is situated two miles west of the Continental Divide, with a significant topographic relief as it rises about 3,000 feet (910 meters) above Pentagon Creek over a one-mile stretch. Precipitation runoff from the mountain flows west and south to the Spotted Bear River through Pentagon Creek and north to the Middle Fork Flathead River via Clack Creek. The nearest higher peak is Three Sisters, located 10.56 miles (16.99 km) to the south. According to the Köppen climate classification, Pentagon Mountain falls within a subarctic climate zone, marked by long, typically very cold winters and short, cool to mild summers, with winter temperatures sometimes dropping below −10 °F and wind chill factors falling below −30 °F. The mountain is composed of sedimentary rock formed in shallow seas during the Precambrian to Jurassic periods. This rock was initially uplifted starting 170 million years ago when the Lewis Overthrust fault moved a massive slab of Precambrian rock—3 miles (4.8 km) thick, 50 miles (80 km) wide, and 160 miles (260 km) long—over younger Cretaceous-period rock.
